sources.title: Execution-Witness Binding: Proof-Carrying Authorization for LLM Agent Runtimes
sources.date_basis: SSRN posting date; paper states date written 2026-02-01 but public posting is used conservatively.
overlap: Separates planning-phase policy evaluation from execution-phase authorization through an execution witness.
Uses one-time execution tokens and deterministic enforcement rather than trusting model behavior.
non_overlap: Does not define availability/consideration/intent/responsibility as independent semantic receipt layers.
Does not span human-AI authorship governance.

sources.title: The Intent Declaration Primitive (IDP) for Agentic AI Systems
overlap: Defines a structured per-transition intent declaration at the moment of agent action.
Treats access permission and declared action intent as different concerns.
non_overlap: Intent declaration is one layer within SOOS and is not the same as the UU-AAP seven-stage chain.
Does not model available-versus-considered intelligence resources.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Delegation in Sovereign Object Systems
overlap: Defines a multi-layer governance architecture with a normative narrowing property for delegated authority.
Composes identity, mandate and execution governance rather than relying on one token.
non_overlap: Its core unit is agent authority over Sovereign Objects, not a general evidence-to-successor semantic stack.
Does not provide one common receipt envelope covering availability, authorship responsibility and outcome semantics.

sources.title: Quantifying Potential Observation Missingness in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
overlap: Formally distinguishes recorded observations from observations that may have been available to the original decision-maker.
Shows that missing decision-time observations can materially change interpretation of an expert action.
non_overlap: Does not separately record whether each available resource was considered or relied upon.
Does not model authority or responsibility as separate from epistemic access.

sources.title: Oplogica v0.2 deterministic verification discipline
sources.date_basis: Repository was created 2026-05-20 and current public repository metadata reports latest push 2026-06-06; current machine-readable discipline therefore predates the Matawaka public anchor under this bounded observation.
overlap: Attaches machine-readable false claims such as verifies_decision_correctness=false, certifies_compliance=false and establishes_fairness=false to verification output.
Uses deterministic overclaim prevention and explicit meaning/not-meaning boundaries.
non_overlap: The block describes one verification result family rather than a shared envelope across heterogeneous semantic receipt types.
It does not define typed transitions among availability, intent, authority, responsibility, action and successor state.

sources.title: An Agent Action Capsule Profile for SCITT
overlap: Separates pre-execution authorization records from the different question of what an agent actually did.
Uses typed dispositions, deterministic constraint records and separate outcome statements.
non_overlap: Does not define availability, consideration or responsibility binding as predecessor receipt layers.
Does not reuse the same semantic stack for authorship governance.

sources.title: Information-flow control: Moving toward secure, autonomous agents
overlap: Uses deterministic system-level controls so permission to invoke a tool does not imply permission for arbitrary information to flow through that action.
Separates data-flow policy from model reasoning and human approval.
non_overlap: Information-flow noninterference is not a general evidentiary semantic composition model.
Does not define cross-domain receipt semantics or availability-versus-consideration.

sources.title: Authorization Evidence Chains: Composing Heterogeneous Agent-Authorization Receipts
overlap: Composes heterogeneous receipt types for one exact action and dispatches each to its own verifier.
Uses a fail-closed requirement expression and explicitly treats identity, delegation, permit, human authorization and transparency as complementary layers.
non_overlap: Composition terminates in authorization-evidence satisfaction for one action rather than a general semantic chain from state/availability through outcome/successor.
Does not model authorship or available-versus-considered intelligence.

sources.title: A SCITT Profile for AI-Agent Action Receipts
overlap: Defines a narrow signed per-action receipt and explicitly states what the receipt does and does not prove.
Separates recorded action/principal/policy/verdict authenticity from correctness, safety, true inputs and real-world outcome.
non_overlap: Negative semantic boundaries are normative prose rather than a common machine-readable non_effects field across receipt classes.
Does not define pre-action availability, consideration, intent and authority-responsibility composition.

sources.title: QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement: Separating Receipt from Authorization for Downstream Effect
sources.date_basis: IETF Internet-Draft -01 publication date observed in bounded search.
overlap: Explicitly specifies that technical receipt does not establish understanding, policy compliance or authority for downstream effect.
Requires separate evidence, policy, freshness and origin checks before downstream release.
non_overlap: It is a specialized receipt-to-effect boundary rather than a general cross-domain receipt calculus.
Does not represent decision resource availability, consideration or responsibility.

sources.title: FAVA: Formal Authorization for Verified Agents with Evidence-Backed Permission Graphs
sources.date_basis: arXiv publication date observed in bounded search.
overlap: Builds an evidence-backed permission graph from structured constraints and data-flow dependencies.
Uses deterministic lowering and SMT verification before any effectful action executes.
non_overlap: Its graph establishes authorization constraints, not the full evidence/availability/intent/responsibility/outcome semantic sequence.
Does not span human-AI authorship governance.
